## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

vec2 uv = vUv;
// subtle chromatic aberration radial
vec2 dir = uv-0.5;

vec3 col;

col.g = texture2D(tDiffuse, uv).g;
col.b = texture2D(tDiffuse, uv - dir*d*0.0025).b;
// vignette
float v = smoothstep(1.05,0.25,d); // ...

col = mix(col, col*vec3(1.08,1.0,0.92), smoothstep(0.45,0.9,luma));

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable, polished Three.js first-person shooter game in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`, continuing from an empty repo. Original request demanded “AAA Call of Duty quality,” which is being interpreted as a highly polished stylized night-ops wave shooter with strong visuals, HUD, audio, and mobile support.

## Requirements
- Build now; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Save screenshot checks as small JPEGs, viewport at most 1280px wide; read only the latest image.
- Use Three.js.
- Deliver a complete playable game, not a prototype.
- Support mobile/touch controls.
- Final response should briefly note assumptions.

## Decisions
- Game concept: “BLACKSITE PROTOCOL,” a rainy industrial port wave-survival FPS with 5 waves, boss wave, score/combo/accuracy stats, health regen, reload/ADS/sprint/jump/crouch, procedural audio, HUD/radar/compass, mobile touch controls.
- Procedural textures and audio only; no external art assets beyond locally vendored Google fonts.
- Vite + Three.js project. Software renderer (`llvmpipe`/SwiftShader) gets a reduced-quality path because full postprocessing/environment maps caused WebGL context loss and ~1 FPS.
- Auto-start capture compatibility: start button has `aria-label="START GAME"`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full project structure: `package.json`, `index.html`, `src/main.js`, `src/style.css`, `src/textures.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/weapon.js`, `src/enemies.js`, `src/effects.js`, `src/physics.js`.
- Built and installed dependencies successfully (`three@0.187.0`, `vite@8.3.6`); `npm run build` passes.
- Implemented procedural world: rainy port yard, walls, containers, crates, barrels, loading dock, catwalk, lamps, signs, puddles, rain, mist, lightning, skyline.
- Implemented detailed first-person rifle model, recoil, ADS, bob/sway, reload animation, muzzle flash, tracers, casings, impact decals/particles.
- Implemented enemies with health/headshot hitboxes, AI movement, LOS, shooting bursts, death animation, boss variant.
- Implemented game flow, waves, scoring, combos, HUD, radar, compass, start/pause/end screens, best score persistence, touch controls.
- Diagnosed WebGL context loss: `RoomEnvironment`/PMREM environment maps kill llvmpipe context; postprocessing is extremely slow; shadows cause transient context loss. Disabled environment, shadows, and post on software; added a low-quality world path.
- Latest change: `buildWorld(scene, renderer, { low: IS_SOFTWARE })` now reduces lights, rain, mist, puddles, skyline, and removes spot/extra point lights on software. Build passes after this change.

### Active
- Testing the new low-quality path for visual quality, FPS, and whether context loss after game start is resolved.

### Blocked
- (none)
